                                        <term_definitions code="at0000">
                                            <items id="text">eGFR</items>
                                            <items id="description">The result, including findings and the laboratory's interpretation, of an investigation performed on specimens collected from an individual or related to that individual.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0001">
                                            <items id="text">Event Series</items>
                                            <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0002">
                                            <items id="text">Any event</items>
                                            <items id="description">Default, unspecified point in time or interval event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run-time.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0003">
                                            <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                            <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0004">
                                            <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                            <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0005">
                                            <items id="text">Test name</items>
                                            <items id="description">Name of the laboratory investigation performed on the specimen(s).</items>
                                            <items id="comment">A test result may be for a single analyte, or a group of items, including panel tests. It is strongly recommended that 'Test name' be coded with a terminology, for example LOINC or SNOMED CT. For example: 'Glucose', 'Urea and Electrolytes', 'Swab', 'Cortisol (am)', 'Potassium in perspiration' or 'Melanoma histopathology'. The name may sometimes include specimen type and patient state, for example 'Fasting blood glucose' or include other information, as 'Potassium (PNA blood gas)'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0017">
                                            <items id="text">Receiving laboratory</items>
                                            <items id="description">Details of the laboratory which received the request and has overall responsibility to manage reporting of the test, even if other labs perform specific aspects.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">This slot is intended to carry details of the laboratory which received the request and has overall responsibility to manage reporting of the test, even if other labs perform specific aspects.

The receiving laboratory may either perform the test or refer it to another laboratory. Where a different laboratory is responsible for performing the testing on specific analytes, it would be expected that these details would be carried in the 'Analyte result detail' SLOT within the CLUSTER.laboratory_test_analyte archetype.

</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0035">
                                            <items id="text">Distribution list</items>
                                            <items id="description">Details of additional clinicians or organisations who require a copy of the test result.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">The 'Distribution list' is for information-only, and that the primary recipient of the report is the person intended to act on the information.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0037">
                                            <items id="text">Partial</items>
                                            <items id="description">This is a partial (e.g. initial, interim or preliminary) Test Result: data in the Test Result may be incomplete or unverified.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0038">
                                            <items id="text">Final</items>
                                            <items id="description">The Test result is complete and verified by an authorised person.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0040">
                                            <items id="text">Amended</items>
                                            <items id="description">The result has been modified subsequent to being Final, and is complete and verified by the responsible pathologist, and result data has been changed.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0057">
                                            <items id="text">Conclusion</items>
                                            <items id="description">Narrative description of the key findings.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: 'Pattern suggests significant renal impairment'. The content of the conclusion will vary, depending on the investigation performed. This conclusion should be aligned with the coded 'Test diagnosis'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0062">
                                            <items id="text">Requester order identifier</items>
                                            <items id="description">The local identifier assigned by the requesting clinical system.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">Equivalent to the HL7 Placer Order Identifier.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0063">
                                            <items id="text">Receiver order identifier</items>
                                            <items id="description">The local identifier assigned to the test order by the order filler, usually by the Laboratory Information System (LIS).</items>
                                            <items id="comment">Assigning an identifier to a request by the Laboratory lnformation System (LIS) enables tracking progress of the request and enables linking results to requests. It also provides a reference to assist with enquiries and it is usually equivalent to the HL7 Filler Order Identifier.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0065">
                                            <items id="text">Specimen detail</items>
                                            <items id="description">Details about the physical substance that has been analysed.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">If the specimen type is sufficiently specified with a code in the Test name, then this additional data is not required. Linking results to specific specimens may be recorded using 'Specimen identifier' elements in both the CLUSTER.specimen and the various results CLUSTER archetypes.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0068">
                                            <items id="text">Laboratory internal identifier</items>
                                            <items id="description">A local identifier assigned by the receiving Laboratory Information System (LIS) to track the test process.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">This identifier is an internal tracking number assigned by the LIS, and it not intended to be the name of the test.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0073">
                                            <items id="text">Overall test status</items>
                                            <items id="description">The status of the laboratory test result as a whole.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">The values have been specifically chosen to match those in the HL7 FHIR Diagnostic report, historically derived from HL7v2 practice. Other local codes/terms can be used via the Text 'choice'.

This element is multiple occurrence to cater for the use cases where statuses for different aspects of the result have been split into several elements.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0074">
                                            <items id="text">Cancelled</items>
                                            <items id="description">The result is unavailable because the test was not started or not completed (also sometimes called 'aborted').</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0075">
                                            <items id="text">Overall test status timestamp</items>
                                            <items id="description">The date and/or time that ‘Overall test status’ was issued.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0077">
                                            <items id="text">Diagnostic service category</items>
                                            <items id="description">The diagnostic service or discipline that is responsible for the laboratory test result.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">This is intended to be a general categorisation and not to capture the organisational name of the laboratory. For example: anatomical pathology, immunology and transfusion medicine, medical microbiology, clinical pharmacology, medical genetics, medical biochemistry. Alternatively more granular sub categories or sub disciplines, such as endocrinology, haematology, and allergology services, may be used. This may assist clinicians in filtering between categories of results. Coding with a terminology is desirable, where possible.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0090">
                                            <items id="text">Requester</items>
                                            <items id="description">Details of the clinician or organisation requesting the laboratory test result.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0094">
                                            <items id="text">Test request details</items>
                                            <items id="description">Details about the test request.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">In most situations there is one test request and a single corresponding test result, however this repeating cluster allows for the situation where there may be multiple test requests reported using a single test result.

As an example: 'a clinician asks for blood glucose in one request and Urea/electrolytes in a second request, but the lab analyser does both and the lab wishes to report these together'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0097">
                                            <items id="text">Test result</items>
                                            <items id="description">Results of the test performed on the specimen(s).</items>
                                            <items id="comment">This SLOT may carry an individual analyte, a group, panel or battery of multiple analytes, or a more complex and specific structure.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0098">
                                            <items id="text">Test diagnosis</items>
                                            <items id="description">Single word, phrase or brief description that represents the clinical meaning and significance of the laboratory test result.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: 'Severe hepatic impairment', 'Salmonella contamination'. Coding of the diagnosis with a terminology is strongly recommended, where possible. This diagnosis should be aligned with the narrative in the 'Conclusion'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0100">
                                            <items id="text">Clinical information provided</items>
                                            <items id="description">Description of clinical information available at the time of interpretation of results.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">This data element may include a link to the original clinical information provided in the test request.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0101">
                                            <items id="text">Comment</items>
                                            <items id="description">Additional narrative about the test result not captured in other fields.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0106">
                                            <items id="text">Original test requested name</items>
                                            <items id="description">Name of the original laboratory test requested.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">This data element is to be used when the test requested differs from the test actually performed by the laboratory.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0107">
                                            <items id="text">Registered</items>
                                            <items id="description">The existence of the test is registered in the Laboratory Information System, but there is nothing yet available.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0110">
                                            <items id="text">Testing details</items>
                                            <items id="description">Structured details about the method of analysis, device or interpretation used.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: 'details of ELISA/nephelometry'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0111">
                                            <items id="text">Point-of-care test</items>
                                            <items id="description">This indicates whether the test was performed directly at Point-of-Care (POCT) as opposed to a formal result from a laboratory or other service delivery organisation.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">True if the test was performed directly at Point-of-Care (POCT).</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0112">
                                            <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                            <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0113">
                                            <items id="text">Confounding factors</items>
                                            <items id="description">Issues or circumstances that impact on the accurate interpretation of the measurement or test result.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">'Confounding factors' should be reserved for uncontrolled/unplanned issues of patient state/physiology that might affect interpretation, for example 'recent exercise' or 'recent tobacco smoking'.

Known or required preconditions, such as 'fasting' should be carried in the 'Sampling conditions' element within the CLUSTER.specimen archetype . In some cases preconditions are captured as part of the test name, for example 'Fasting blood glucose'.

Known issues with specimen collection or handling, such as 'prolonged use of tourniquet' or 'sample haemolysed', should be carried in the 'Specimen quality' elements within CLUSTER.specimen archetype.

Coding with a terminology is desirable, where possible.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0114">
                                            <items id="text">Structured confounding factors</items>
                                            <items id="description">Details of issues or circumstances that impact on the accurate interpretation of the measurement or test result.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: Last Normal Menstrual Period (LNMP).</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0115">
                                            <items id="text">Corrected</items>
                                            <items id="description">The result has been modified subsequent to being Final, and is complete and verified by the responsible pathologist. This is a sub-category of 'Amended'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0116">
                                            <items id="text">Entered in error</items>
                                            <items id="description">The Test Result has been withdrawn following previous Final release.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0117">
                                            <items id="text">Extension</items>
                                            <items id="description">Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0118">
                                            <items id="text">Multimedia representation</items>
                                            <items id="description">Digital image, video or diagram representing the test result.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">Multiple formats are allowed but they should represent equivalent clinical content.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0119">
                                            <items id="text">Appended</items>
                                            <items id="description">Subsequent to being final, the report has been modified by adding new content. The existing content is unchanged. This is a sub-category of 'Amended'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0120">
                                            <items id="text">Preliminary</items>
                                            <items id="description">Verified early results are available, but not all results are final. This is a sub-category of 'Partial'.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0121">
                                            <items id="text">Test method</items>
                                            <items id="description">Description about the method used to perform the test.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">Coding with a terminology is desirable, where possible.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0122">
                                            <items id="text">Structured test diagnosis</items>
                                            <items id="description">A structured or complex diagnosis for the laboratory test.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: Anatomical pathology diagnoses consisting of several different axes such as morphology, etiology and function.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                    </children>

                                        <term_definitions code="at0000">
                                            <items id="text">Body surface area</items>
                                            <items id="description">The measured or calculated surface area of a human body.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">May also be referred to as BSA.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0001">
                                            <items id="text">Event Series</items>
                                            <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0002">
                                            <items id="text">Any event</items>
                                            <items id="description">Default, unspecified point in time or interval event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run-time.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0003">
                                            <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                            <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0004">
                                            <items id="text">Body Surface Area</items>
                                            <items id="description">The measured or calculated surface area of a human body.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: '1.81 m2'</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0005">
                                            <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                            <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0006">
                                            <items id="text">Formula</items>
                                            <items id="description">Formula used to calculate the BSA.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: Mosteller, DuBois and DuBois, Haycock and Boyd.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0007">
                                            <items id="text">Extension</items>
                                            <items id="description">Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.</items>
                                            <items id="comment">For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0008">
                                            <items id="text">Device</items>
                                            <items id="description">The device used to measure or estimate the body surface area.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0009">
                                            <items id="text">Method</items>
                                            <items id="description">The method by which the body surface area was entered into the clinical system.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0010">
                                            <items id="text">System entry</items>
                                            <items id="description">The Area was entered automatically by the clinical system and without manual intervention of the clinician.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0011">
                                            <items id="text">Manual entry</items>
                                            <items id="description">The Area was entered manually by the clinician.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0012">
                                            <items id="text">Dubois and Dubois</items>
                                            <items id="description">The Dubois and Dubois formula was used to calculate the body surface area.</items>
                                        </term_definitions>
                                        <term_definitions code="at0013">
                                            <items id="text">Mosteller</items>
                                            <items id="description">The Mosteller formula was used to calculate the body surface area.</items>

                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0142">

                                                </term_definitions>

                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0159">

                                                <archetype_id>
                                                    <value>openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.dosage.v1</value>
                                                </archetype_id>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0000">
                                                    <items id="text">Original Dosage</items>
                                                    <items id="description">The combination of a medication amount and administration timing for a single day, in the context of a medication order or medication management.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: '2 tablets at 6pm' or '20mg three times per day'. Please note: this cluster allows multiple occurrences to enable representation of a complete set of dose patterns for a single dose direction.</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0037">
                                                    <items id="text">Daily timing</items>
                                                    <items id="description">Structured details about the timing pattern for a single day.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'in the morning', 'at 0600, 1400, 2100'.</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0102">
                                                    <items id="text">Administration duration</items>
                                                    <items id="description">The period of time over which a single dose of the medication or vaccine should be administered.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'Administer over 10 minutes'.</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0134">
                                                    <items id="text">Administration rate</items>
                                                    <items id="description">The rate at which the medication, such as an infusion, is to be administered.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: '200 ml/h'. Use the text data type to record non- or semi-quantifiable instructions.</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0135">
                                                    <items id="text">Dose formula</items>
                                                    <items id="description">The formula used to calculate the dose amount or administration rate where this is dependent on some other factor, such as body weight or surface area.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: '10mg/kg/day'. The result of this formula would normally be held in Dose amount/unit or Administration rate/duration. Where clinical measurements such as body weight is used in the dose calculation, a LINK attribute should used to specify which particular measurement has been used.</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0144">
                                                    <items id="text">Dose</items>
                                                    <items id="description">The value of the amount of medication administered at one time, as a real number, or range of real numbers, and associated with the Dose unit.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: 1, 1.5, 0.125 or 1-2, 12.5-20.5</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0145">
                                                    <items id="text">Unit of measure</items>
                                                    <items id="description">The unit which is associated with the Dose amount.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'tablet','mg'. Coding of the dose unit with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0164">
                                                    <items id="text">Dosage sequence</items>
                                                    <items id="description">The intended position of this dosage within the overall sequence of dosages.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example: '1', '2', '3'. 
Where multiple dosages are expressed, the 'Pattern sequence' makes the order in which they should be executed explicit. For example: (1) 1 tab in the morning, (2) 2 tab at 2pm, (3) 1 tab at night.</items>
                                                </term_definitions>
                                                <term_definitions code="at0176">
                                                    <items id="text">Alternate dose amount</items>
                                                    <items id="description">An alternate representation of the value of the amount of medication administered at one time, as a real number, or range of real numbers, and associated with the Dose unit.</items>
                                                    <items id="comment">For example, can be used to represent a unit-dose based value such as 'tabs', when the Dose amount is expressed as an SI unit such as 'mg', or where it is required to express the total amount of an infusion as well as the dose amount of the active ingredient.</items>

                                <term_definitions code="at0000">
                                    <items id="text">Medication management</items>
                                    <items id="description">Any activity related to the planning, scheduling, prescription management, dispensing, administration, cessation and other use of a medication, vaccine, nutritional product or other therapeutic item.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">This is not limited to activities performed based on medication orders from clinicians, but could also include for example taking over the counter medication.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0002">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription issued</items>
                                    <items id="description">A prescription has been issued for the medication.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0003">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription dispensed</items>
                                    <items id="description">The ordered medication has been dispensed, for example from a pharmacy to the patient.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0004">
                                    <items id="text">Medication course commenced</items>
                                    <items id="description">The medication has been taken by, or administered to, the patient for the first time. Although in some settings this significant date may be computable as the first of several administrations, in other settings, such as primary care, specific administration dates are not readily available.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0005">
                                    <items id="text">Medication reassessed</items>
                                    <items id="description">The individual medication has been reassessed, for example whether the medication should still be taken. This is not intended to capture review of the medication list.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0006">
                                    <items id="text">Dose given</items>
                                    <items id="description">A single administration of the medication has taken place.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0007">
                                    <items id="text">Medication course completed</items>
                                    <items id="description">The medication course has been completed as planned.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0008">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription supply delayed</items>
                                    <items id="description">The prescription has not been dispensed due to a technical or pharamaceutical supply issue.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0009">
                                    <items id="text">Administrations suspended</items>
                                    <items id="description">The administration of the medication has been suspended until further notice. No further doses should be given until the restart date or conditions have been met. When setting the date/conditions for restart after suspending, a step from ‘Administrations suspended’ and back to 'Medication start date/condition set' should be performed.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0010">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription re-issued</items>
                                    <items id="description">A prescription has been re-issued for an existing medication order.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0011">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription re-authorisation pending</items>
                                    <items id="description">Issue of the prescription is awaiting re-authorisation by a clinician.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0012">
                                    <items id="text">Medication course cancelled</items>
                                    <items id="description">The planned course of medication has been cancelled prior to any administration.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0013">
                                    <items id="text">Medication course postponed</items>
                                    <items id="description">The scheduled medication course has been postponed prior to any administration.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0015">
                                    <items id="text">Medication course stopped</items>
                                    <items id="description">Administration of the medication has been ceased during the period of the intended course.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0016">
                                    <items id="text">Medication start date/condition set</items>
                                    <items id="description">The time to start the medication, or other starting condition, has been set.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0017">
                                    <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0018">
                                    <items id="text">Dose not given</items>
                                    <items id="description">An administration of the medication has been withheld and not given. There is no expectation that it will be given later, though the next dose (if any) should be administered according to the original order.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0020">
                                    <items id="text">Medication name</items>
                                    <items id="description">Name of the medication, vaccine or other therapeutic/prescribable item which was the focus of the activity.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'Atenolol 100mg' or 'Tenormin tablets 100mg'. 
It is strongly recommended that the 'Medication item' is coded with a terminology capable of triggering decision support, where possible. The extent of coding may vary from the simple name of the medication item through to structured details about the actual medication pack used. Free text entry should only be used if there is no appropriate terminology available.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0021">
                                    <items id="text">Reason non attendance</items>
                                    <items id="description">Reason that the pathway step for the identified medication was carried out.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'Postponed - Patient not avalable at administration time', 'Cancelled - Adverse reaction'. Note: This is not the reason for the medication instruction, but rather the specific reason that a care step was carried out, and will often be used to document some variance from the original order.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0024">
                                    <items id="text">Note</items>
                                    <items id="description">Additional narrative about the activity or pathway step not captured in other fields, including details of any variance between the intended action and the action actually performed.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'Patient was in radiology department', 'Accidental injection into blood vessel during IM administration'.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0025">
                                    <items id="text">Sequence number</items>
                                    <items id="description">The sequence number specific to the pathway step being recorded.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0030">
                                    <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0033">
                                    <items id="text">Patient guidance</items>
                                    <items id="description">Any guidance, instructions or advice given to the subject of care or personal carer at the time of the pathway step.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'Avoid grapefruit' , 'Take at least 2 hours before bedtime', 'Take with food'. May be coded with a terminology when clinically appropriate.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0039">
                                    <items id="text">Major change to order</items>
                                    <items id="description">A major change to the order was required, resulting in this order being stopped and a replacement order being started.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0041">
                                    <items id="text">Minor change to order</items>
                                    <items id="description">The medication order has been changed in a manner which does not require a new instruction/order to be issued, according to local clinical rules.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0043">
                                    <items id="text">Original scheduled date/time</items>
                                    <items id="description">The datetime at which the medication action was scheduled to occur.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Used to compare variance from actual action time where this is not readily calculable from the original instruction.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0044">
                                    <items id="text">Dose administration deferred</items>
                                    <items id="description">An administration of a dose of the medication has been delayed but is expected to be given as soon as possible.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0053">
                                    <items id="text">Additional details</items>
                                    <items id="description">Further structured details of the action, possibly specific to a pathway step.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0085">
                                    <items id="text">Extension</items>
                                    <items id="description">Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0103">
                                    <items id="text">Order ID</items>
                                    <items id="description">Unique identifier for the medication order.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Comment: This data element allows for multiple occurrences to be defined more explicitly at run-time, if required.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0104">
                                    <items id="text">Medication details</items>
                                    <items id="description">Structured details about the medication including strength, form and constituent substances.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Use this SLOT where the detailed description of the dispensed, authorised or administered item needs to be explicitly stated. For example: the form, strength, any diluents or mixture of ingredients.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0106">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription re-authorised</items>
                                    <items id="description">The original medication order has been re-authorised to allow repeat prescription or dispensing. In some jurisdictions an entirely new order must be issued in these circumstances.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0109">
                                    <items id="text">Medication recommended</items>
                                    <items id="description">The medication has been recommended but no steps have been taken to initiate prescribing.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0131">
                                    <items id="text">Amount</items>
                                    <items id="description">Specific details about the amount of the medication item.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">CLUSTER.dosage is intended to carry details of medication order changes or dose administrations, whilst CLUSTER.medication_supply_amount is intended for details of dispensing-related activity.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0132">
                                    <items id="text">Substitution</items>
                                    <items id="description">Subsitution action taken by the person administering or dispensing the drug.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">In many jurisdictions, substitution of an ordered item as a generic form or with a different brand name, which has been determined as bioequivalent, is allowed at the point of dispense or supply. In other cases substitution is assumed and the clinician has to explicitly request non-substitution.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0133">
                                    <items id="text">Substitution reason</items>
                                    <items id="description">The reason or justification for the substitution action taken.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: "Generic alternative contains a substance that is not tolerated by the patient." May be coded with a terminology when clinically appropriate</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0138">
                                    <items id="text">Substitution performed</items>
                                    <items id="description">A medication was substituted which is bioequivalent to that ordered.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0139">
                                    <items id="text">Substitution not performed</items>
                                    <items id="description">Although allowed by the medication order a bioequvalent medication was not substituted.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0140">
                                    <items id="text">Administration details</items>
                                    <items id="description">Details of body site and administration of the medication.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0141">
                                    <items id="text">Body site</items>
                                    <items id="description">Structured description of the site of administration of the ordered item.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: 'left upper arm', 'intravenous catheter right hand'. 
Coding of the body site with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0142">
                                    <items id="text">Structured body site</items>
                                    <items id="description">Structured description of the site of administration of the medication, vaccine or therapeutic good.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: "On the medial skin surface of the left forearm, from 10 cm to 20 cm distally from the point of the elbow".</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0143">
                                    <items id="text">Administration method</items>
                                    <items id="description">The technique or device by which the ordered item was, or is to be, administered.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Comment: For example: ' via Z-track injection'; 'via nebuliser'. Coding of the method with a terminology is preferred, where possible.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0144">
                                    <items id="text">Administration device</items>
                                    <items id="description">Details of the medical device used to assist administration of the medication.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0145">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription awaiting authorisation</items>
                                    <items id="description">Draft prescription has been prepared and is awaiting confirmation from an authorised clinician. May be used where reauthorisations are performed as a batch. This careflow_step may have a status of 'planned' or 'active', reflecting the need to to handle new orders as well as re-authorised orders.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0147">
                                    <items id="text">Route</items>
                                    <items id="description">The route by which the ordered item was, or is to be, administered into the subject's body.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Comment: For example: 'oral', 'intravenous', or 'topical'. Coding of the route with a terminology is preferred, where possible. Multiple potential routes may be specified.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0148">
                                    <items id="text">Medication prepared</items>
                                    <items id="description">The medication has been physically prepared. For example: preparation of an intravenous mixture.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0149">
                                    <items id="text">Double-checked?</items>
                                    <items id="description">The pathway step has been checked by a separate individual.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Details of the individual performing the double-check can be carried in the Reference Model element "Participation".</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0150">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription cancelled</items>
                                    <items id="description">The prescription was cancelled prior to being issued.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0151">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription invalid or expired</items>
                                    <items id="description">Prescription has been invalidated or has expired without being fulfilled.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0152">
                                    <items id="text">Prescription fulfilled</items>
                                    <items id="description">The prescription has been fulfilled successfully.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0153">
                                    <items id="text">Medication authorised</items>
                                    <items id="description">The medication has been formally authorised for use.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0154">
                                    <items id="text">Restart date/time</items>
                                    <items id="description">The date/time on which the medication course is set to restart, as per the "Administrations suspended" pathway step.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: 2017-10-29</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0155">
                                    <items id="text">Restart criterion</items>
                                    <items id="description">The criterion which triggers the medication course to restart, as per the "Administrations suspended" pathway step.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: "On day 2 after surgery".</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                            </children>

request.description:
This call allows the uploading of an openEHR `operational template` generated by openEHR modelling tools such as the [openEHR Archetype Designer](https://tools.openehr.org/designer/).

The Postman request will automatically update the current `templateId` Environment variable if successful.

##### Response Messages

```
201  Success.

400  Invalid content (unable to read opt) (TMPL-3602).

401  Unauthenticated - could not authenticate user (SYS-9401).

403  Forbidden - the user does not have the required permissions to execute this request (SYS-9403).
```
##### Typical output
```json
{
    "action": "CREATE",
    "templateId": "NES-ACP_COVID.v0.0"
}

                                    <value>openEHR-EHR-EVALUATION.precaution-risk_info_era.v1</value>
                                </archetype_id>
                                <term_definitions code="at0000.1">
                                    <items id="text">Risk info</items>
                                    <items id="description">A condition or state of the individual that is clinically significant and unique or idiosyncratic for this individual, and is considered vital information when making treatment decisions.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0.1">
                                    <items id="text">Additional information</items>
                                    <items id="description">*</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0.2">
                                    <items id="text">ABO Blood Group</items>
                                    <items id="description">*</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0.3">
                                    <items id="text">Rhesus Blood Group</items>
                                    <items id="description">*</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0000">
                                    <items id="text">Precaution</items>
                                    <items id="description">A condition or state of the individual that is clinically significant and unique or idiosyncratic for this individual, and is considered vital information when making treatment decisions.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0001">
                                    <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0002">
                                    <items id="text">Risk description</items>
                                    <items id="description">Identification, by name, of a condition or state.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Coding of the identified 'Condition' with a terminology is desirable, where possible.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0003">
                                    <items id="text">Evidence</items>
                                    <items id="description">Description of the evidence identified to support the precaution.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">This data element can be optionally linked to a diagnosis, test result, medication order etc via a URI (as per the Reference Model) in order to provide the rationale or evidence for the precaution assertion. Please note: as this URI link may not be accessible from a message or by receiving clinical system it is desirable that a narrative description of the evidence should also be explicitly recorded.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0004">
                                    <items id="text">Last updated</items>
                                    <items id="description">Date when the precaution information was last updated.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0006">
                                    <items id="text">Tree</items>
                                    <items id="description">@ internal @</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0008">
                                    <items id="text">Instructions for treatment</items>
                                    <items id="description">Additional narrative about the precaution, not captured in other fields.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0009">
                                    <items id="text">Review date</items>
                                    <items id="description">Date when next due for review by a clinician.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">In circumstances where precautions are not indefinite or life-long, use this data element to record the date/time when this precaution should be reassessed in the context of the clinical circumstances at the time.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0013">
                                    <items id="text">Risk type</items>
                                    <items id="description">Type of the 'Condition' identified.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">This data element has been included because it is currently being captured in some clinical systems. This information could be derived when terminology codes are used to represent the condition in clinical systems, and is effectively redundant in that situation.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0014">
                                    <items id="text">Status</items>
                                    <items id="description">Assertion about the current state of the identified 'Precaution'.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">Decision support would typically raise alerts for 'Active' and ignore a 'Resolved' or 'Refuted' precaution. Clinical systems may choose not to display Precaution entries with a 'Refuted' status in the Precaution list. However, 'Refuted' may be useful for reconciliation of the Precaution list or when communicating between systems. Some implementations may choose to make this field mandatory. 'Resolved' may be used variably across systems, depending on clinical use and context. The free text data type will allow for local variation by enabling other value sets to be applied to this data element in a template - in this situation it is recommended that values should be coded using a terminology.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0015">
                                    <items id="text">Active</items>
                                    <items id="description">The precaution is currently active.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0018">
                                    <items id="text">Resolved</items>
                                    <items id="description">The previously asserted precaution has been clinically reassessed and considered no longer to be an active risk.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0019">
                                    <items id="text">Refuted</items>
                                    <items id="description">The precaution has been clinically reassessed or has been disproved with a high level of clinical certainty by testing.</items>
                                </term_definitions>
                                <term_definitions code="at0020">
                                    <items id="text">Extension</items>
                                    <items id="description">Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms.</items>
                                    <items id="comment">For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents.</items>
                                </term_definitions>

item.name: Get web template JSON - Better CDR only

request.description:
Returns an openEhr template in its web-appropriate representation (as a JSON object). 

A note on languages: the web template will be generated with localized names for all the languages that the underlying template supports, unless it is specified differently via the defaultLanguage and languages query parameters, both of which are optional. 

The defaultLanguage parameter determines the default name for each web template node (the localizedName property), whereas the languages parameter will generate additional localized names inside the localizedNames map for all the languages listed in this parameter (different languages should be separated by a comma: en,sl,no). 

Note that the underlying openEhr template needs to support these languages, or else a 400 error (bad request) will be returned (TMPL-3061).

response.name: Get web template JSON

request.description:
Resource Url

https://ehrscape.code-4-health.org/rest/v1/template/{templateId}/example
Parameters

Parameter  Value  Description  Parameter Type  Data Type
templateId
required
  The ID of the template to load.  path  string
defaultLanguage
optional
  The default language to generate the web template with.  query  string
languages
optional
  Other languages to include in the web template, separated by a comma.  query  string
format
optional

The format of JSON representation of the example composition to return. Default: FLAT.  query  enum
exampleFilter
optional

The type of example to produce - intended for input (sent to the server), output (received back from the server) etc.  query  enum
Try it out!
Implementation Notes

Returns an example of data values for a ThinkEhr web template.

This method will show all the web template paths that can be filled out in order to successfully save a composition in the web template format. It will do its best to generate legal exampledata values for those paths, taking into account the data type and validation constraints.

Two parameters control the output of this call. The format parameter controls whether the produced output will be the web template composition values in either the FLAT or the STRUCTURED (hierarchical) JSON format. The exampleFilter parameter controls whether the example will show the values as they would be submitted to the server (INPUT) or received from the server (OUTPUT), since the latter one is more detailed.

The two language parameters determine the languages that the web template will be generated with before its example values will be produced and returned. See the documentation for the {templateId} call for more information on web template languages.

request.description:
Resource Url

https://ehrscape.code-4-health.org/rest/v1/template/{templateId}/example

Parameters

Parameter  Value  Description  Parameter Type  Data Type
templateId
required
  The ID of the template to load.  path  string
defaultLanguage
optional
  The default language to generate the web template with.  query  string
languages
optional
  Other languages to include in the web template, separated by a comma.  query  string
format
optional

The format of JSON representation of the example composition to return. Default: FLAT.  query  enum
exampleFilter
optional

The type of example to produce - intended for input (sent to the server), output (received back from the server) etc.  query  enum
Try it out!
Implementation Notes

Returns an example of data values for a ThinkEhr web template.

This method will show all the web template paths that can be filled out in order to successfully save a composition in the web template format. It will do its best to generate legal exampledata values for those paths, taking into account the data type and validation constraints.

Two parameters control the output of this call. The format parameter controls whether the produced output will be the web template composition values in either the FLAT or the STRUCTURED (hierarchical) JSON format. The exampleFilter parameter controls whether the example will show the values as they would be submitted to the server (INPUT) or received from the server (OUTPUT), since the latter one is more detailed.

The two language parameters determine the languages that the web template will be generated with before its example values will be produced and returned. See the documentation for the {templateId} call for more information on web template languages.

Resource Url

https://ehrscape.code-4-health.org/rest/v1/template/{templateId}/example
Parameters

Parameter  Value  Description  Parameter Type  Data Type
templateId
required
  The ID of the template to load.  path  string
defaultLanguage
optional
  The default language to generate the web template with.  query  string
languages
optional
  Other languages to include in the web template, separated by a comma.  query  string
format
optional

The format of JSON representation of the example composition to return. Default: FLAT.  query  enum
exampleFilter
optional

The type of example to produce - intended for input (sent to the server), output (received back from the server) etc.  query  enum
Try it out!
Implementation Notes

Returns an example of data values for a ThinkEhr web template.

This method will show all the web template paths that can be filled out in order to successfully save a composition in the web template format. It will do its best to generate legal exampledata values for those paths, taking into account the data type and validation constraints.

Two parameters control the output of this call. The format parameter controls whether the produced output will be the web template composition values in either the FLAT or the STRUCTURED (hierarchical) JSON format. The exampleFilter parameter controls whether the example will show the values as they would be submitted to the server (INPUT) or received from the server (OUTPUT), since the latter one is more detailed.

The two language parameters determine the languages that the web template will be generated with before its example values will be produced and returned. See the documentation for the {templateId} call for more information on web template languages.

request.description:
Saves a new openEHR composition to the specified patient EHR.

The composition can be in one of the supported formats (FLAT, STRUCTURED, RAW or TDD). Unless the `format` parameter is RAW, the `templateId` parameter is required. The composition data is sent in the request body.

EHR ID: The EHR to save the composition into, needs to be specified via the `ehrId` parameter.


##### Response Messages
```
201	Successfully created - response body will contain a link to the newly created composition	
400	Bad request - could not parse the format parameter (COMP-1011), templateId not specified (TMPL-3031), no EHR to save to can be determined (EHR-2031), composition language and territory problems (COMP-1051, COMP-1061, COMP-1071), invalid composition data (COMP-1081).
401	Unauthenticated - could not authenticate the user (SYS-9401).
403	Forbidden - the user does not have the required permissions to execute this request (SYS-9403).
404	EHR with the given ID does not exist (EHR-2021), template with the given ID does not exist (TMPL-3021).
```

request.description:
Saves a new openEHR composition to the specified patient EHR.

The composition can be in one of the supported formats (FLAT, STRUCTURED, RAW or TDD). Unless the `format` parameter is RAW, the `templateId` parameter is required. The composition data is sent in the request body.

EHR ID: The EHR to save the composition into, needs to be specified via the `ehrId` parameter.


##### Response Messages
```
201	Successfully created - response body will contain a link to the newly created composition	
400	Bad request - could not parse the format parameter (COMP-1011), templateId not specified (TMPL-3031), no EHR to save to can be determined (EHR-2031), composition language and territory problems (COMP-1051, COMP-1061, COMP-1071), invalid composition data (COMP-1081).
401	Unauthenticated - could not authenticate the user (SYS-9401).
403	Forbidden - the user does not have the required permissions to execute this request (SYS-9403).
404	EHR with the given ID does not exist (EHR-2021), template with the given ID does not exist (TMPL-3021).
```

item.description: The `compositionId` environment variable is updatedautmatically after a successful POST (201).

request.description:
Returns an openEHR composition denoted by the specified ID in one of the supported formats, along with some metadata.

The ID can be specified as a complete unique ID with the domain and version part (8849182c-82ad-4088-a07f-48ead4180515::ehrscape.com::1), or just the identifier part (8849182c-82ad-4088-a07f-48ead4180515), in which case the last version of the composition will be returned.

##### Response codes
```
200	Success - returns composition data and meta-data in response body.	
204	No content - requested composition has been deleted. In this case, the HTTP response will contain a Link header giving the URL to the last active (non-deleted) version of the composition.
400	Could not parse the format parameter (COMP-1011).
401	Unauthenticated - could not authenticate the user (SYS-9401).
403	Forbidden - the user does not have the required permissions to execute this request (SYS-9403).
404	Composition with the given ID does not exist (COMP-1021).
```

request.description:
Returns an openEHR composition denoted by the specified ID in one of the supported formats, along with some metadata.

The ID can be specified as a complete unique ID with the domain and version part (8849182c-82ad-4088-a07f-48ead4180515::ehrscape.com::1), or just the identifier part (8849182c-82ad-4088-a07f-48ead4180515), in which case the last version of the composition will be returned.

##### Response codes
```
200	Success - returns composition data and meta-data in response body.	
204	No content - requested composition has been deleted. In this case, the HTTP response will contain a Link header giving the URL to the last active (non-deleted) version of the composition.
400	Could not parse the format parameter (COMP-1011).
401	Unauthenticated - could not authenticate the user (SYS-9401).
403	Forbidden - the user does not have the required permissions to execute this request (SYS-9403).
404	Composition with the given ID does not exist (COMP-1021).
```

request.description:
Returns the EhrStatus object associated with a specific subjectID and subject Namespace.

##### Parameters

###### `subjectId`

This is the external identifier by which the patient is known within the CDR. It is normally a real-word identifier like an NHS number, CHI number or Hoptial 'MRI' number, and will have been supplied to the CDR when the patients' `EHR` object was created in the datastore.

Example value : `9999999000`

###### `subjectNamespace`

This is just a unique string used to identify the numbering scheme used for the 'subjectId'. It will commonly be some sort of URI such as `uk.nhs.nhs_number` and will have been agreed at national level.

Example value : `uk.nhs.nhs_number`
